proof_sketch: For the twist-free diagonal metric g = g_B + sum p_I^2 d phi_I^2, the vertical Ricci trace satisfies tr_h Ric^V = sum_I (-Delta_B p_I/p_I - sum_{J!=I} <grad p_J, grad p_I>/(p_J p_I)). Meanwhile, w = prod p_I gives -Delta_B w / w = -sum_I Delta_B p_I/p_I - sum_{I!=J} <grad p_I, grad p_J>/(p_I p_J). These are identical because Delta(product)/product = sum Delta p_I/p_I + sum_{I!=J} <grad p_I, grad p_J>/(p_I p_J), which follows from the product rule applied to log w = sum log p_I: Delta w/w = Delta(log w) + |grad log w|^2 = sum (Delta p_I/p_I - |grad p_I|^2/p_I^2) + sum_{I,J} <grad p_I, grad p_J>/(p_I p_J). The |grad p_I|^2/p_I^2 terms cancel against the I=J terms in the double sum, leaving Delta w/w = sum Delta p_I/p_I + sum_{I!=J} <grad p_I,grad p_J>/(p_I p_J).

all_dimensional_note: The identity tr_h Ric^V = -Delta_B w/w holds for any base dimension m and fiber dimension k, in the twist-free diagonal case. For m=2 Faber-Krahn gives a base area lower bound without needing base Ricci bounds. For m>=3, converting eigenvalue bounds to volume bounds requires additional base curvature control that is NOT automatic from total-space Ricci pinching.
twist_note: For k=2 with twist, Step 12 verified tr_h Ric^V = -Delta w/w + |F|^2/2. The twist potential is nonneg, so lambda_1^Dir <= k(1+delta) survives. General k with twist has not been symbolically verified but the structural argument extends: twist contributes a nonneg potential to the Schrodinger operator.
key_result: For any T^k-invariant n-manifold (n=k+m) with positive Ricci pinching delta < 1, the orbit-space Dirichlet eigenvalue satisfies k(1-delta) <= lambda_1^Dir(Omega, g_B) <= k(1+delta). This pins the orbit space spectral scale in all dimensions.
limitation: The T^k identity requires an actual isometric T^k action. General metrics have no torus symmetry. The general-to-invariant reduction is the load-bearing open bridge.
